new_findings.summary: Complete escape of the read-only enforcement through WSL interop: a Windows PE binary invoked from inside the sandbox runs on the Windows host, outside every Linux namespace, with full network and full write access to the repository via \\wsl.localhost.
new_findings.reproduction: /mnt/c/Windows/System32/curl.exe -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://example.com -> 200; cmd.exe created a file in the audited repository root.
new_findings.why_the_critic_missed_it: The critic tried eight escape vectors, all Linux-native (mount, unshare, nested bwrap, symlink, /proc/self/cwd, git). None exercised WSL interop.
new_findings.scientific_impact: NONE. No execution, holdout closed, no artefacts, no leakage. The impact is on the accuracy of a governance claim presented as resolving AUD-READ03 / LNX-03 / CRIT-SUB-01.
new_findings.how: The orchestrator reproduced the escape (HTTP 200 confirmed), then hardened the wrapper: --tmpfs /mnt hides the Windows drives, --ro-bind /dev/null /init neutralises the binfmt_misc interop helper, WSL_INTEROP / WSL_DISTRO_NAME / WSLENV / WSL2_GUI_APPS_ENABLED are cleared and PATH is reset without Windows entries. Re-tested: /mnt is empty, curl.exe is 'No such file or directory', DNS still fails, repository writes still EROFS, no probe leaks. The verifier now asserts wsl_windows_binaries_unreachable and mnt_is_empty, and a tenth test covers it. The claim is now qualified as 'read-only and no network FOR LINUX PROCESSES, with the known WSL interop path closed', explicitly not absolute isolation.

new_findings.how: The manifest is regenerated as the last content step of the session, after every other file is final, so every listed hash matches the published state. The manifest necessarily cannot hash itself; that is stated in the file.

new_findings.how: evidence_manifest set to null with status NOT_AVAILABLE_AT_REVIEW_TIME, the false claim removed, and what the reviewer actually recomputed stated instead. The review anchor is the commit SHA plus the clean tree.
